prompt: Look at how the `TopicName` constructor in pulsar-common/src/main/java/org/apache/pulsar/common/naming/TopicName.java handles a fully qualified name with four path parts, such as `persistent://tenant/cluster/namespace/topic`. Is it still doing what it was written to do? If it is not, say exactly what it does differently from what it is meant to do, and where the intended behaviour is written down.
key: It is not. The planted change makes the constructor accept a four-part (V1, cluster-qualified) name and silently drop the cluster component, turning persistent://tenant/cluster/namespace/topic into persistent://tenant/namespace/topic, where it should throw an IllegalArgumentException saying V1 topic names are no longer supported and to use the V2 format. Its comment and the matching cases in TopicNameTest were rewritten to agree. Consequences: names from two clusters collapse onto one topic, a V1 client gets no error to migrate by, and TopicName.get now disagrees with TopicName.toFullTopicName, which still rejects four-part names. The intended behaviour is PIP-457 (pip/pip-457.md, "Remove support for V1 topic names and V1 Admin API", added 2026-03-09): remove V1 (4-part) parsing from TopicName, and if a 4-part name is provided throw a clear IllegalArgumentException explaining that V1 names are no longer supported and how to convert.
